summary: Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University and with traditional teachers Seungsahn and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, later serving as Director of the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center (attested 2007–2013).
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under doctoral supervisor Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, holding a post at Deakin University. He studied under advisers Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, as well as traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche.
Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held posts at Utrecht University (~1964–1975) and served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1975–1998).

Peter Gyallay-Pap works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the London School of Economics and Political Science by 1990 and was an adjunct at Adams State University (attested 2007).

Peter Harvey works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996 and was attested as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland from 2002 to 2015.
Peter Haskel specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter James Gilks works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from Australian National University (attested 2010) under John Powers, and studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under traditional teachers including Geshe Ngawang Jangchup and Tsultrim Phuntsok.

Peter Koret is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who completed a doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter M. Scharf (b. 1957) is an Indologist and linguist. He completed his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, and also studied under Shree Narayan Mishra, Ludo Rocher, and Narendranath Pandey.
Peter Masefield specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Charles F. Keyes, also studying under traditional teachers Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Choga Rinpoche.

Peter N. Gregory (b. 1945) works in Buddhist studies and sinology. After receiving his PhD from Harvard (1981) under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held posts at the Kuroda Institute, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and Smith College.
Peter Schwabland works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Washington under supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Peter Schwieger (b. 1952) is a scholar of Tibetology. He studied under Dieter Schuh (~1972–1978), succeeded Klaus Sagaster in 2001, and served as Professor at the University of Bonn (~2002–2018).

Peter Skilling works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études by 2004. He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and taught at Chulalongkorn University and École française d'Extrême-Orient (2009).

Peter Stewart (b. 1971) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. In 2011, he held posts at the Classical Art Research Centre and as Associate Professor of Classical Art and Archaeology at the University of Oxford.

Peter Zieme (b. 1942) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held posts at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (~1965–1991), Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1992–2007), and Free University of Berlin.

Peter van der Veer (b. 1953) studied at Groningen and Utrecht universities. Active in religious studies, Indology, and sinology, he held posts at Utrecht University (~2000–2018) and served as Director at the Max Planck Institute (~2009–2021).

Peter von Bohlen (1796–1840) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Bonn under Georg Wilhelm Freytag, and Berlin under Franz Bopp, before becoming außerordentlicher Professor at the University of Königsberg in 1826.
